newsitem.title: ITALY: Italian employers say welfare talks wasting time.
newsitem.headline: Italian employers say welfare talks wasting time.

text.p: Talks aimed at introducing a reform of the Italian welfare state are not moving forward, and time is running out, the chairman of the Italian employers' federation Confindustria said on Tuesday.
"We are basically at the same point where we were a month ago," Giorgio Fossa told reporters after a meeting between government, unions and employers.
Despite Fossa's comments, union leaders said earlier on Tuesday progress had been made in the welfare talks and a union-backed solution looked possible when talks resumed next month.

Prime Minister Romano Prodi launched a welfare review in mid-June and Tuesday's meeting was the last before the summer break. Talks will resume on August 28, with the government looking to reach a deal by the end of September.

"We have lost almost a month and a half. From August 28, we'll have only a few days to tackle this problem," Fossa said. "We are in a situation of uncertainty....The only thing which gives us some hope is that the reform will have to be contained in the 1998 budget."
The 1998 budget must be unveiled by September 30.
